corrected_text: In our build and in the release Agello ships, the C API's conversation stream callback (CreateConversationCallback in c/conversation.cc) turns the first error status it receives into a final chunk with the error text, or the empty message into a final chunk without error, and then drops every later message, error or not (ours: 8acc748c); a send therefore gets one final chunk however many terminal events the conversation layer produces.
note: Re-pin 2026-11-17, meaning changed: CreateConversationCallback at b7b856a0 and 6da75396 (c/conversation.cc:45-86, identical) keeps a shared atomic 'ended': the first !ok or empty message exchanges it to true, and every later call returns at once (comment: 'one final chunk per send'). Commit 8acc748c (2026-10-24, 'C API: one final chunk per conversation send [4.1b]'). The stateless v0.18.0 callback is gone from the shipped build.

corrected_text: In our build and in the release Agello ships, for a Gemma 4 conversation with tools in its preface, one tool-call block that the FC parser rejects is reported to the C layer's callback as an error at least twice for the same send: when the block's end fence streams, the internal callback's SendMessage passes the failed ToMessage status (InvalidArgument, because return_error_on_parse_failure defaults to true and neither the C API nor Swift changes it) and decoding goes on; at the end of decode SendCompleteMessage parses the whole reply again and fails on the same block. The C stream callback passes on only the first as a final error chunk and drops the rest (ours: 8acc748c).
note: Re-pin 2026-11-17, meaning changed at the C layer: internal_callback_util.cc (SendMessage 61-71, the fence branch 447-466, the end branch 330-343, SendCompleteMessage 95-149), data_utils.cc, parser_utils.cc and model_data_processor.h are unchanged from base in both b7b856a0 and 6da75396; gemma4_data_processor.cc:146-155 as cited; return_error_on_parse_failure_ still defaults to true (conversation.h:278, model_data_processor.h) and nothing in c/ or swift/ sets it (git grep). The 2026-11-17 Gemma 4 tool commits (9a84a518, 586e2e4c) change the template and the first token after a tool response, not this path. New: CreateConversationCallback (c/conversation.cc:45-86) ends after the first error, so only one final chunk reaches the binding (8acc748c); its comment says a rejected call can report up to three errors (a failing flush of unsent text in SendCompleteMessage adds one), hence 'at least twice'.

corrected_text: In the Swift wrapper of our build and of the release Agello ships, each native send of a stream finds its StreamContext through StreamTable by an integer ID passed as callback_data, not a retained pointer: an error chunk or the final chunk retires the ID, the context finishes the stream once (later finishes do nothing), and a chunk for a retired ID returns without touching anything (ours: 4ca2cf33). A second terminal chunk for the same send can't reach freed memory; the C layer also sends only one (ours: 8acc748c).
note: Re-pin 2026-11-17, the gap is closed: swift/ConversationStream.swift at b7b856a0 (new file, 4ca2cf33, 2026-10-16, also in 6da75396): StreamContext.finish ends once under a lock (101-159); StreamTable registers IDs that are never reused and retires them (221-255); handleStreamChunk returns when the ID has no entry, retires it on an error or a final chunk, and finishes the context (273-336); sendToStream registers the context and passes UnsafeMutableRawPointer(bitPattern: id) as callback_data (Conversation.swift:623-639). The release's files differ only in a header comment and 'sending' on yield. The C callback's 'ended' flag (8acc748c) drops later finals as well.

corrected_text: The other terminal paths of the conversation layer deliver one terminal event per send: SendCompleteMessage returns after reporting an extraction or parse error without sending the end sentinel; the internal callback's error, cancelled, failed and token-limit-error branches each make one user callback and return; and in our build, when the channel-filter refill reports an error itself, the deferred end sentinel is suppressed.
note: Re-pin 2026-11-17, wording only: internal_callback_util.cc:95-149 and 292-343 unchanged from base; runtime/conversation/conversation.cc:749-770 and 775-834 at b7b856a0 as cited (the 2026-11-17 commits there add the Gemma 4 template fix and the first-token bans after a tool response, not terminal paths).

corrected_text: In the Swift wrapper of our build and of the release Agello ships, a non-final chunk whose text isn't valid JSON or doesn't convert to a Message retires the send's ID, finishes the stream with the error and cancels the native work; later chunks of that send find no entry and are dropped (ours: 4ca2cf33).
note: Re-pin 2026-11-17, the gap is closed: handleStreamChunk (swift/ConversationStream.swift:273-304 at b7b856a0 and 6da75396) catches a JSON or jsonToMessage failure, calls StreamTable.retire(id), and 'if context.finish(throwing:) { context.cancelNativeWork() }'; a later chunk's context(for: id) is nil and returns at line 276.

corrected_text: Agello streams chat replies with Conversation.sendMessageStream on conversations that declare CurrentDateTimeTool and CalculatorTool when tools are enabled and WebSearchTool when options.webSearchTool is set, so in those chats a tool-call block that the parser rejects reaches the rejected-tool-call path; in the release Agello ships, that path ends the stream once, with the first error.
note: Re-pin 2026-11-17: Agello at a6912128 (2026-11-17) still builds the chat conversation with [CurrentDateTimeTool(), CalculatorTool()] when tools are on and appends WebSearchTool() when options.webSearchTool (ChatEngine.swift:399-400), and streams with sendMessageStream (876-881). The 'two-error-chunk path of the shipped wrapper' is gone: the release's C callback sends one final chunk (8acc748c) and its wrapper finishes a stream once (4ca2cf33).
